gomoku.description: Five stones in a row — straight, diagonal, anywhere on the board — before your opponent does.

download.heading: Download the app

trust.heading: Trust & Fair Play
trust.body: The server decides every result — never the client. Every match can be independently replayed and verified. Funds under review are held, never confiscated, until a person signs off.
trust.point_server_body: The client can never assert a result, a score, or a clock reading — only the server does.
trust.point_verify_body: Every finished match can be re-run from its own recorded moves and checked against the result.
trust.point_human_body: No automated action ever restricts funds or an account on a single weak signal — a person decides.

rank.heading: Global Skill Breakdown
rank.subtitle: How your score is actually built, game by game.
rank.empty: Establish a rating in at least one game to see your breakdown.
rank.breadth_note: Playing multiple games well adds a +{breadth}% breadth bonus, capped so no single game can carry your score alone.
rank.methodology_body_1: Only games where you've played at least 10 rated matches and your rating has settled down count toward your score. Each counts by percentile rank among other established players of that same game -- not your raw rating -- so Chess and Speed Math are directly comparable.
rank.methodology_body_2: Each game's weight comes from how much you've played it and how confident that rating is, capped at 35% so no single game can dominate the total. A small bonus rewards genuine skill spread across several games.

learnPage.heading: Learn
learnPage.subhead: How Nizalo actually works, and the rules for every game.
learnPage.how_body: Every action you take is sent to the server as a request, never as a claimed fact. The server alone applies the rules, keeps the clock, and decides the result. That is what makes a match here replayable and independently checkable — nothing about the outcome depends on trusting either player's device.
learnPage.games_body: Pick a game to see how it's played, timed, and scored.
learnPage.fair_body: Timing and behaviour are checked automatically, but no single automated signal ever restricts an account or holds funds — that decision always goes to a person, with the evidence in front of them.
learnPage.fair_cta: Read the full Fair Play policy →

fairPlayPage.heading: Trust & Fair Play
fairPlayPage.subhead: What actually keeps a match fair here — stated plainly, not marketing language.
fairPlayPage.server_heading: The server is the only authority
fairPlayPage.server_body: A player's device can only ever send a request — "I'd like to play e4" — never a claimed fact. Legality, the clock, the score, and the result are all decided entirely on the server. There is no message a client can send that asserts an outcome.
fairPlayPage.verify_body: A finished match's real, recorded moves can be replayed from the start and checked against the result that was paid out. This is the same check used internally before any dispute is resolved — it does not depend on trusting a database value.
fairPlayPage.review_heading: Money decisions are never fully automated
fairPlayPage.review_body: Timing and behaviour are monitored, but no single automated signal ever restricts an account or holds funds on its own. A statistical finding is always sent to a person to review before any action is taken, and every such action can be appealed to a different reviewer.
fairPlayPage.eligibility_body: Where competitive play involves a prize, participation and any resulting prize are subject to eligibility rules that vary by region. Nizalo is a game of skill — not an investment, and never a guaranteed income.
